job.title: Accounts Payable Officer
job.description:
About the Role

We are currently recruiting multiple AO3 Accounts Payable Officers to join a large and busy government finance team based in Toowoomba.

These opportunities will see you working within a high-volume transactional finance environment, supporting the accurate and timely processing of payments and financial transactions while managing queries, resolving processing issues and ensuring work is completed within required timeframes.

With multiple positions available and potential contracts through to May 2027, this is a great opportunity for experienced Accounts Payable professionals looking to build further experience within State Government.

Key Responsibilities
  • Undertake high-volume Accounts Payable and transactional processing accurately and efficiently
  • Monitor and prioritise work queues to meet required deadlines and service standards
  • Identify, investigate and resolve processing errors and discrepancies
  • Respond to payment and finance queries from internal and external stakeholders
  • Escalate complex issues where required and ensure appropriate follow-through
  • Maintain accurate financial information and data across multiple systems
  • Work collaboratively with team members to manage changing priorities and high-volume periods
  • Contribute to improvements in transactional processes and procedures
These responsibilities reflect the client's focus on accurate end-to-end transactional processing, prioritising work queues, resolving errors, responding to stakeholder queries and supporting the wider team during periods of increased volume.

About You
  • Previous experience in Accounts Payable, transactional finance or finance administration
  • Experience working in a fast-paced, high-volume processing environment
  • Strong numerical skills with excellent accuracy and attention to detail
  • Confidence working across multiple computer and finance systems
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Ability to prioritise competing workloads and meet deadlines
  • A collaborative and positive approach to working within a team
  • Initiative and the ability to work independently when required
Previous experience within State Government, local government or a similar public sector finance environment would be highly regarded. SAP or similar large ERP system experience would also be advantageous.

What’s in it for you?
  • Multiple positions available
  • $51.12 per hour + 12% superannuation
  • Potential contract through to May 2027
  • Full-time hours, Monday to Friday
  • Toowoomba-based opportunity
  • Join a large and established government finance team
  • Collaborative and supportive working environment
  • Build valuable State Government experience
  • Opportunity to further develop your high-volume Accounts Payable experience

job.title: Senior Designer (Civil)
job.description:
We are seeking a highly skilled Senior Civil Designer (PO6) to join a major QLD State Government Department on the Sunshine Coast to support the planning and design of complex road and civil infrastructure projects.

About this role
In this role you, reporting to the Principal Advisor (Design) the Senior Designer will work autonomously across civil design activities while collaborating with other designers, engineers and project stakeholders.

You will be responsible for developing and delivering civil design solutions that meet project objectives, technical standards and stakeholder requirements.
  
Key responsibilities  
  • Undertake civil design and drafting using 12D and AutoCAD for road and transport infrastructure projects.
  • Develop, prepare and quantify transport infrastructure design models across strategic planning, concept, development and implementation phases.
  • Manage key components of the planning and design process to support successful project delivery within agreed time, cost, quality and stakeholder expectations.
  • Investigate, analyse and conceptualise potential design options to determine practical and effective solutions.
  • Apply appropriate design processes and methodologies based on individual project requirements and delivery strategies.
  • Ensure designs are developed in accordance with relevant legislation, policies, standards, specifications and technical guidelines.
  • Assist with the technical review of transport infrastructure design drawings, models and documentation prepared by external design consultancies.
  • Identify potential design risks, evaluate possible solutions and implement appropriate mitigation strategies.
  • Contribute technical knowledge and experience to support the development and capability of other members of the design team.
About you
To be successful, you will be able to demonstrate:
  • Previous experience in a Senior Designer or Design Management positions.
  • Previous experience in delivering civil designs appropriate for construction (intersections, widening, highways, etc)
  • Previous experience in developing and quantifying transport infrastructure design models.
  • Tertiary qualifications in Engineering (min 2 year Dublin Accord accredited or recognised equivalent)
  • Extensive experience using and experience in using 12D and AutoCAD software.
  • Make informed technical decisions and exercise sound judgement regarding when issues require escalation.
  • Ability to remain focused and effective in environments involving competing priorities, ambiguity and change, whilst making considered, ethical and well-informed decisions
  • Ability to communicate effectively with designers, engineers, project managers, consultants and other stakeholders.
  • Hold a current White Card (or able to obtain)
Previous experience in a similar role within Government or similar complex organisation would be highly beneficial. Additional experience across large Capital Works infrastructure projects (hospitals, schools, stadiums etc) will be highly desirable.

What this role offers you
  • Up to $103 per Hour + 12% Superannuation

  • Collaborative, high-performing project environment

job.title: AO7 Principal Planner
job.description:
Shape the future of Queensland’s regions!

Queensland is growing, and this is an opportunity to play a key role in planning for that growth!

The Queensland Government has committed to an ambitious program of delivering new regional plans, supported by infrastructure plans, across every corner of Queensland as part of its commitment to deliver one million homes by 2044.

We are seeking an experienced AO7 Principal Planner to join the Regional Planning Division and contribute to the development, review and implementation of regional plans that will help shape sustainable, well-planned and connected communities across Queensland.

The opportunity

As a Principal Planner, you will be part of a multidisciplinary team responsible for reviewing and implementing regional plans under the Planning Act 2016 and the Regional Planning Interests Act 2014.
You will lead and contribute to regional planning workstreams, undertaking research, analysis, mapping and technical investigations to inform high-quality, evidence-based regional planning policy.

A key part of the role will be building productive relationships with a diverse range of stakeholders. You will work closely with other state government agencies, local governments, infrastructure providers, community representatives, industry peak bodies and technical experts to understand the opportunities, challenges and infrastructure needs of Queensland’s growing regional communities.
You will also provide strategic advice on complex regional planning matters and brief Regional Planning leadership on key findings, emerging issues and recommended approaches.

What you’ll bring
To succeed in this role, you will demonstrate:
  • Research and analytical capability – Strong research, data analysis and evidence-based decision-making skills, with the ability to translate complex information into practical planning and policy outcomes.
  • Policy development and writing skills – The ability to prepare high-quality policy documents, regional plans, supporting guidance, correspondence and briefing materials for a range of audiences.
  • Strategic thinking and problem-solving – The ability to analyse complex planning policy and development assessment matters and develop considered, practical responses within a regional planning context.
  • Leadership – The capability to lead regional planning workstreams, coordinate research and analysis, brief senior leadership on findings and provide sound advice on complex and sensitive issues.
  • Stakeholder engagement – The confidence and interpersonal skills to build effective relationships and work collaboratively across government, local councils, industry, infrastructure providers, communities and technical disciplines.
  • Preferred background in working with or exposed to - RPS, Urbis, Local Councils, Urban Utilities.
About the team:

The Regional Planning Division brings together people with diverse professional skills and experience across planning policy, ecology, housing, urban design, demographics, data analytics, spatial analysis and policy implementation.
You’ll join a collaborative team working on planning issues that have a direct impact on Queensland’s future growth, housing, infrastructure and regional communities.

What this role offers you:
  • $88 - $94 per Hour, plus 12% Superannuation
  • 12 month initial assignment, with possibility of extension
  • 40 hours per week, Monday to Friday
  • Easily accessible via public transport, Brisbane CBD location
  • Weekly pay cycles, with no payroll fees
  • Expert public sector consultants to support you throughout your assignment

job.title: Senior Environmental Officer (PO4)
job.description:
Kingston Human Capital are currently supporting a Gold Coast based public sector organisation with the appointment of a Senior Environmental Officer (PO4).

The Coomera Connector Stage 1 (Coomera to Nerang) team is responsible for completing the design, environmental referral, site investigations and review to support the delivery of the Coomera Connector project.

Reporting to the Project Manager, the role will be responsible for supporting environmental approvals, compliance, environmental management and sustainability outcomes throughout the project lifecycle.

The successful Senior Environmental Officer will also contribute to the environmental governance, stakeholder engagement and reporting  to internal executives
  
What you will be doing
Some of your key responsibilities will include:
  • Provide high-level specialist advice regarding statutory obligations under relevant Commonwealth, State and local environmental legislation, regulations, policies and approval frameworks, including requirements under the Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Act 1999 (EPBC Act).
  • Support the planning, preparation, coordination and delivery of Commonwealth and State environmental approvals, permits, conditions and environmental offsets, ensuring project activities remain aligned with applicable legislative and regulatory requirements.
  • Review and provide technical input into project designs, environmental assessments, environmental surveys, spatial and ecological data, Public Environment Reports (PERs), environmental management documentation and associated technical studies.
  • Review contract documentation, technical specifications, environmental conditions, approval packages, audit documentation and project briefs to ensure environmental requirements are appropriately incorporated into project delivery.
  • Identify and assess potential environmental constraints, impacts, risks and opportunities and work collaboratively with project teams and technical specialists to develop appropriate avoidance, mitigation and management measures.
  • Work with design and delivery teams to negotiate and recommend design modifications or alternative solutions where required to address environmental constraints and approval conditions.
  • Support environmental assurance activities, including the review and coordination of environmental audits, inspections, compliance assessments.
  • Prepare and review high-quality technical reports, correspondence, briefing materials, recommendations, presentations and executive advice relating to environmental matters and broader project delivery requirements.
  • Represent the project at working groups, steering committees, technical forums, stakeholder meetings and other internal and external meetings, clearly communicating environmental requirements, risks, decisions and agreed actions.
  
What this role offers you
  • 12-month initial assignment, with possibility of extension
  • 37.5 hours per week, Monday to Friday
  • Easily accessible from the motor way (M1) or the internal Gold Coast | onsite parking available
  • Weekly pay cycles, with no payroll fees
  • Expert public sector consultants to support you throughout your assignment
  
Mandatory Requirements:
  • A Degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Environmental Management or Natural Resource Management from a recognised tertiary institution or equivalent qualification is mandatory.
  • Current holder of a 'C' class driver’s licence.
  • Criminal history screening will be conducted on the recommended person for this role.
